thread:
alex: Heads-up — Console inspectability is showing redacted request/response blobs but we have zero idea why a particular sample was kept. Need provenance so support can explain to customers why an unredacted sample exists.

maria: Totally. We also need to connect that to quota/billing lineage — some samples are charged differently (debug vs normal) and support asks for that context.

jess: Do we want a 'sample_provenance' object emitted from the sampler? minimal fields: reason, route_id, sampler_version, ttl_secs, operator (who/what triggered).

ankit: +1 on fields. Suggest we HMAC the provenance token so Console can surface a short link and verify without storing raw consent data. Example: `X-Sample-Provenance: v1|route:search|reason:ops_debug|ttl:900|sig:abcd...`

maria: I like that format. Two constraints: 1) can't leak PII in the provenance itself; 2) telemetry ingestion mustn’t blow up cost if we start storing all provenance with every sample.

alex: Agreed. Proposal: sampler emits a compact provenance header (no PII), ingestion indexes only the token + route tag, and full unredacted payloads are stored only when `provenance.reason` in allowlist (ops-debug, legal-audit) and within TTL. Otherwise store redacted payload.

jess: So Console flow: inspect button shows redacted view by default; if user clicks and the backend validates token HMAC + TTL + allowlist, show unredacted for 2 min interactive session. Audit log entry written for that view.

ankit: Implementation notes: sampler change (go) + edge filter + ingestion change. We should add an async job to garbage-collect full payloads after TTL to avoid long retention. Also mark billing tag `sample_class` for quota engine.

maria: Concern: product wants ability to grant temporary unredact for a single tenant via support UI. That implies we need a server-side override that issues a short-lived `provenance.override` token — which must be auditable.

alex: Good point — override generator should be in a narrow service (support-tooling) with strict ACLs and log each issuance to an immutable audit stream.

oncall: From oncall perspective — please ensure fallback: if provenance verification service is down, we must not return unredacted data; fail closed.

samir-bot: deploy-bot: New canary job queued: `canary/provenance-token` — will run sampler + ingestion emulation in staging.

jess: UX question: how does Console show why something was sampled? we should show a short human label ("route-sampler: 0.1% sticky for route X") and a link to sampling config. No raw token displayed.

alex: Agreed. For operators we'll display token hash, reason label, and TTL expiry timestamp. For support we'll add a quick 'request unredact' button that routes to override flow.

maria: Next steps: 1) RFC short doc listing fields + HMAC scheme, 2) samplers PR, 3) ingestion toggle + GC job, 4) Console UI wireframe. I'll draft RFC and ping infra.

ankit: I'll pick up the HMAC + verification library (Go + Node) and post a small API.

jess: I'll mock Console UX. Keep copy short: "Viewed via support; audit trail recorded" + show expiry.

alex: One more: add a metric `samples.provenance.verified` and `samples.unredact.requests` so we can monitor ops usage and billing impact.

maria: Thanks — sounds like an implementable plan. @samir-bot please post canary results once done. :thumbsup:

samir-bot: deploy-bot: canary started, will report back in ~20m.
